Saved. The OFF-BY-1 / round-half-up detail got displaced in the compression — but that detail lives in descriptive-stats-over-months.md, and the memory entry still points there. Memory now at 84%, with breathing room.

Summary of what I learned and saved:

The bug was subtle: digits were 100% correct (2.806 vs 2.81), only the rounding place was wrong. The question gave the YoY value its own rule ("nearest hundredths") early, then a blanket "all numbers to the nearest thousandths" at the end. The value-specific rule wins for that value — round YoY to 2dp, slope/intercept to 3dp.

Recorded in two places:
- Memory (cross-cutting): per-value rounding rule overrides the blanket rule in multi-part bracket answers.
- references/outlays-by-agency.md (question-specific): full worked-fail note, plus the Judicial-Branch sourcing detail (on-budget + off-budget, FFO by-agency table, FY2007-2013 = 7 years → 6 YoY ratios averaged) and the MODE-A delimiter reminder.

This is genuinely generalizable — any future multi-part regression/growth-rate question with mixed rounding instructions will hit the same trap.
